extracted.intended_audience: web authors, content creators, and accessibility/web developers at Penn State (instructors or staff who publish math on Penn State sites)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical how-to guidance for enabling accessible MathML display and MathJax on web pages and common CMS (Sites at Penn State, WordPress, Drupal) including generation, embedding, styling, and screen-reader considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use MathML for accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML is important for accessibility and web standards because it allows equations to be stored as structured text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathML can be reformatted with CSS, expanded with good resolution for low-vision users, and—most importantly—if a screen reader can process MathML, a blind user can navigate and review parts of an equation, such as the top portion of a complex fraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use MathJax to enable correct MathML display
rubrics_metrics.description: MathJax is a set of open-source JavaScript libraries which enable correct display of MathML content in browsers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a link to the MathJax library in the HEAD or appropriate location. For a public page use the CDN link example provided; for password-protected pages use the HTTPS version. In the MathJax Configuration select 'TeX-AMS-MML_HTMLorMML'. Note: if you use a link with a config option you may need to add 'MathJax.js?' before the string '/config'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the MathML namespace in <math>
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'namespace' refers to incorporating a link to the MathML specification typically in a tag such as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The link enables some browsers to process MathML more accurately. When copying sample MathML into editors or pages, include the namespace link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'm namespace' MathML unless necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: "m namespace" refers to an earlier MathML variant used by Microsoft; only Internet Explorer ever recognized it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended to avoid using m namespace MathML unless there is an issue of backwards compatibility with a particular student. In m namespace MathML tags include a prefix m: (e.g. <m:math>) or possibly mml:.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use display="block" for standalone equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the attribute display="block" to the MATH tag if you want the equation to be on its own line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove the attribute if you want to embed the MathML in a sentence. Example: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block">

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure MathML-capable fonts are available
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to view MathML, a browser should have a MathML font installed which includes symbols used to build different equation types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some freeware fonts include Cambria Math (may be present on systems), STIX 2 font, Asana Math. Check system/browser font availability if symbols render poorly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test with supported browsers and screen readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost all modern browsers support native MathML, although MathJax adds additional utilities for users. Modern versions of screen readers support MathML to differing degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2025, the combination of NVDA with the MathCat plugin is a good choice for testing. Verify rendering and navigability with the assistive technologies your audience uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate MathML using equation editors that export MathML
rubrics_metrics.description: The most efficient way to generate MathML is to use an equation editor such as MathType (Windows), MathMagic (Mac/Windows), or other equation editor which supports MathML export.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: The built-in Microsoft Office equation editor does not fully support MathML, but it can import MathML content from other equation editors which support MathML. Equatio can export MathML, but not edit it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import MathML into equation editors by copy/paste
rubrics_metrics.description: Many equation editor tools 'import' MathML in the editor window by pasting MathML code; the program will convert the code to a visual equation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sample MathML code (e.g., provided fraction example) as a test case to confirm successful import and conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check export options in your equation editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult instructions for an equation editor to determine if exporting or saving as MathML is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different editors have different levels of support—confirm that the tool you use can export the MathML you need for publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert LaTeX to MathML when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use LaTeX, use a tool which converts LaTeX to MathML such as Equatio, MathType, MathMagic or other online conversion utilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the conversion output and adjust as necessary, since automatic conversion can introduce layout or semantic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply CSS to MathML but be mindful of MathJax interference
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply inline CSS attributes to both the MATH tag and individual tags (e.g. MFRAC, MROW, MO and others). However, MathJax interferes with that mechanism somewhat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With MathJax enabled you can either apply inline styles to MathML tags or create custom classes. Examples: inline <math style="font-size:1.5em"> or custom classes like div.mathd {font-size:1.5em} and mfrac.red {color:#C00}.

rubrics_metrics.name: When using CMS plugins, configure MathJax plugin correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: You can embed MathML, but you must enable the MathJax plugin (example instructions provided for Sites at Penn State).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include activating the MathJax-LaTeX plugin, possibly deactivating/reactivating if activated before October 2014, opening Settings, unchecking Use MathJax CDN Service if required, entering a Custom MathJax Location (e.g., https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/mathjax/2.7.0/MathJax.js), selecting TeX-AMS-MML_HTMLorMML in MathJax Configuration, and saving changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed MathML in posts/pages using [mathjax] tags and no blank lines
rubrics_metrics.description: To add MathML to a Post or Page: create/open a Page/Post, click the Text tab to enter code view, and where you want to insert MathML enter [mathjax] ... [mathjax].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy and paste MathML code with namespace link between the two tags. Make sure that there are no blank lines in the MathML code. Publish and View to verify content.

rubrics_metrics.name: When using Jetpack/WordPress, style MathJax output classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of applying CSS to MathML tags, you need to apply CSS to MathJax plugin classes (e.g. .MathJax_Display).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Jetpack plugin is activated (requires a WordPress.com account) and target the plugin's output classes for styling rather than raw MathML tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable MathML via system configuration for other CMS (Drupal, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML can be automated in many platforms such as Drupal and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check with your system administrator to learn how MathML support is enabled on your institutional CMS; administrators can contact accessibilityweb@psu.edu for assistance.
